bull_bear.body:
- brand: DNEG's standing as a high-end independent VFX and animation house — evidence: DNEG has won 8 Academy Awards, 8 BAFTA Awards, 26 Visual Effects Society Awards and 4 Primetime Emmy Awards — against it: the MD&A flags platform consolidation increasing pricing pressure and margin compression across content, animation and service providers
- scale: one of India's largest integrated production facilities — evidence: Prime Focus Studios in Mumbai's Film City covers approximately 200,000 square feet with eight purpose-built sound stages and a seven-acre backlot
- scale: round-the-clock 'world sourcing' delivery network — evidence: operates across 4 continents, 7 time zones and 24 locations, enabling work on projects 24/7, with about 94.26% of revenue from international markets
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Industry risk — shifting consumer preferences, regulation and industry strikes — The Company says the constantly changing media industry can affect profitability and long-term growth, and that strikes or disruptions can hit production schedules, delay deliveries and reduce operational efficiency.
- Competition risk, intensified by AI — Intense competition from domestic and international players; rapid AI advances make content creation and production easier and faster, increasing competitive pressure on the Company's market position.
- Talent retention risk — Business depends on skilled human resources; attrition, shortage of skilled talent and the limited number of institutes offering VFX training create hiring challenges and risk of losing talent to competitors.
- Profitability risk — low-margin industry — The Company notes the M&E industry operates on relatively low margins; delays in content releases and rising costs of hiring skilled professionals add financial pressure.
- Cyber security risk — Data breaches, ransomware, phishing and targeted attacks could impact IT infrastructure, business operations and sensitive data as digitalisation increases.
- Client commissioning cyclicality at global studios — The MD&A notes the Hollywood writers' strike disrupted global entertainment supply chains and that international studios prioritised fewer high-value film and television projects in 2025.

outlook.body:
- AI is reshaping how content is created, distributed, discovered and monetised across the M&E value chain, extending beyond cost efficiencies to content creation, personalisation and advertising.
- Advertising is expected to remain the fastest-growing M&E revenue category, overtaking consumer spending as the largest growth category in 2026, aided by digital consumption and AI-enabled targeting.
- Streaming growth is expected to moderate as mature markets face subscription fatigue; platforms are shifting to ad-supported tiers, bundles and partnerships to improve monetisation and reduce churn.
- Demand for in-person entertainment (cinema, live music, trade shows) is increasing, with global box office projected to grow at a 3.5% CAGR to US$ 39.5 billion by 2030.
- Traditional television remains under structural pressure from digital alternatives.
- Indian M&E industry reached approximately `2.78 trillion in 2025, growing 9%, with digital media the largest segment; industry expected to grow at an over-7% CAGR to approximately `3.3 trillion by 2028.
- VFX remained the largest segment of Indian animation/VFX/post-production, with studios adopting AI-driven workflows to manage pricing pressures caused by leaner production pipelines.
- Indian animation softened on slower global commissioning, lower kids-focused advertising and reduced OTT commissioning hours, while the overall animation/VFX/post-production market showed early signs of recovery and stabilisation in 2025.
- Multi-language programming by OTT platforms and broadcasters (typically 5 to 7 languages) and nearly 200,000 hours of content produced in India support demand for editing, dubbing, subtitling and localisation.
- Digital rights and broadcast rights values declined on OTT consolidation and pressure on TV ratings and advertising revenues.
